To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we detected 10 dusty disks around stars in the 2 Myr old cluster IC348 with the Submillmeter Array, (2) these disks are the faintest millimeter detections of protoplanetary systems to date, and (3) these faint millimeter sources may represent the best candidate systems in the cluster to form planets in proportion to the field.

the number of small grains in the disks in the 1 Myr old cluster IC 348 is much less than the number in the 1-2 Myr old T Tauri stars in Taurus and Ophuchus and that these faint millimeter continuum sources in IC 348 may represent the best place to study the transition from planetesimals into planets.

the disk mass distribution in IC348 is shifted by about 20 times to lower values compared to Taurus and Oph, that this shift occurs within 1 Myr, and that the IC348 disks are likely the best candidates in young clusters for the formation of planets.

the evolution of the small dust grains in circumstellar disks and their role in the formation of planets.
the formation of planets and the early stages of star and planet formation.
the formation and evolution of planetary systems and is a step toward understanding the initial conditions and processes of planet formation in the early stages of stellar evolution.
